The use of topsoil and fertilizer if necessary will accelerate this process, but it will still take much time to regain the sustained capability that now exists on the better soils. However, much of the area, particularly in areas of Wibaux and Midway soil series, does not have good soils at present, and the reclamation program may actually improve the productivity of the land by redistributing the soil resource.
Analysis of overburden samples showed high levels of sodium in some areas of the lower strata near the Robinson Coal seam. Due to the method of strip mining proposed by Westmoreland, this material will probably be placed near the top of the spoils. If this occurs, there may be problems with reclamation. The mixing action during the mining process and the later contouring program is expected to dilute this excess sodium to a certain extent. Where available topsoil is not sufficient to mitigate adverse soil properties, adequate neutral fill will be provided. However, the placement of high sodium materials nearer the surface than they now exist constitutes an adverse impact since they may be exposed by erosion or penetrated by plant root systems. Land Use and Productivity
There are 30,876.45 acres in Tracts II and III. Within Tract II there are 350,000,000 tons of mineable coal and Tract III contains 850,000,000 tons. If all of the coal is mined, approximately 25,000 acres of land will be disturbed on both tracts. This represents a large acreage, but it must be remembered that reclamation will be going on concurrently with the mining activity.
